title: docs: MCP_SERVER.md complete_task currentBranch note and moe-qa-loop SKILL.md step 3 describe shared-mode landing only
description:
Filed by WT-19's whole-epic adversarial review (task-b1ca54f2716442be889a14623eb59983, step 7).

PROBLEM. Two doc passages still describe only shared-mode landing.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md, the complete_task currentBranch note. It says the wrapper lands "on the branch its safe-branch step picks (a literal consolidationBranch doubles as that peel target; otherwise moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD>)". In worktree mode that is wrong:
  - the worker reports moe/task/<taskId>;
  - the completion is a merge-tree squash onto the target (a literal consolidationBranch, else main);
  - no safe-branch step runs.
- docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md step 3. It says "`git branch --contains <sha>` confirms it is on the shared branch". In worktree mode the completion SHA is on the target.

EVIDENCE. Checked on merged tree 88e507e5 (moe/work-2026-10-24 at 1558f141 plus the WT-19 task).
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md:587. The correct worktree bullet sits two lines up, at :585.
- docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md:26.
- The wrapper side: scripts/moe-agent.sh:7726, "Never peel_target_branch, ensure_safe_branch or the shared push".

IMPACT. Since WT-19's gate-aware default, a project with a qualityGate runs in worktree mode. A QA seat or an integrator following these lines checks the wrong branch. It may reject a correctly landed task, or chase a moe/work-<date> branch that never moves.

FIX DIRECTION. Add a worktree-mode clause to both passages, naming the target (a literal consolidationBranch, else main) and the branch (moe/task/<taskId>). Rebuild the daemon in a snapshot so prebuild re-vendors the skill. The same kind of doc drift is already filed as task-347dde8560ac467aaa9c02a1d1532b74, and one session can take both.

implementationPlan.description: DoD 1 - docs/MCP_SERVER.md complete_task currentBranch bullet. Rewrite ONLY the bullet that starts '`currentBranch` is reported by the agent (the CLI), not by the wrapper' (docs/MCP_SERVER.md:587; the WT-02 worktree branch rule sits two lines up at :585 and the branch-policy bullet at :586 - leave both untouched). Keep the shared-mode sentence word for word, now scoped to shared mode, and add a worktree clause. Suggested text: '- `currentBranch` is reported by the agent (the CLI), not by the wrapper: the wrapper's landing happens *after* this call. In shared mode it lands on the branch its safe-branch step picks (a literal `consolidationBranch` doubles as that peel target; otherwise `moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD>`). In worktree mode the agent reports its task branch `moe/task/<taskId>` (the WT-02 rule above), no safe-branch step runs, and the completion lands as one `merge-tree` squash commit on the target: a literal `consolidationBranch`, else `main`. In both modes the branch it actually landed on arrives afterwards as `record_commit.ref` / `task.commits[].ref` (`refs/heads/<target>` for a worktree completion). That is why an absent `currentBranch` warns instead of failing.' Source facts (verified at planning): scripts/moe-agent.sh land_worktree_completion (~7757-7765) uses target=${CS_CONSOLIDATION_BRANCH:-main} and falls back to main when the value holds ? or [; read_commit_settings (~3128) already turns a * glob into empty; the ps1 twin Invoke-MoeWorktreeCompletion (~7251) falls back to main the same way; the completion is recorded with record_commit_rpc ... completion ... refs/heads/$target (~7794/7801); moe-agent.sh:7726 says 'Never peel_target_branch, ensure_safe_branch or the shared push'. So 'literal' means no *, ? or [. Constraints: daemonGitDocs.test.ts scans every docs/*.md line, so never write a phrase like 'never runs git', 'does not run git', 'runs no git' or 'never touches git'. The chat_read section (~2519) belongs to task-b2f95099 (REVIEW): do not touch it. Use the Edit tool only, never a shell write (mem:gotcha-docs-edit-via-bash-python-no-tool-witness); edit in your task worktree (git rev-parse --show-toplevel), never in /mnt/d/projexts/moes (mem:decision-doc-row-checkrefs-worktree-mode). Error handling: a doc-only step with no runtime path; a wrong claim is caught by the step-5 cross-check against the wrapper code, and the test gate is step 4.

implementationPlan.description: DoD 2 (text half) - docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md step 3 (line 26). Replace only the clause '`git branch --contains <sha>` confirms it is on the shared branch.' with a per-mode statement of where the completion lands, for example: '`git branch --contains <sha>` confirms it is on the branch the entry's `ref` names: in shared mode the shared branch; in worktree mode the target (a literal `consolidationBranch`, else `main`, recorded as `refs/heads/<target>`), where the wrapper squash-lands the task branch `moe/task/<taskId>`.' Leave every other byte of step 3 unchanged, including the mode test already in it ('worktree mode: `git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name HEAD` prints exactly `refs/heads/moe/control`; otherwise shared mode'). Do not claim which OTHER branches lack the SHA: a LANDING-CONFLICT resume merges the target into moe/task/<taskId>, so 'not on the task branch' can turn false. qaCommitPolicy.test.ts pins this file AND its vendored copy (the SENTINELS, ROUTE_SENTINELS, FORBIDDEN and RETIRED lists at the top of packages/moe-daemon/src/util/qaCommitPolicy.test.ts): keep every pinned phrase ('bounded wait, not a blocker', 'up to ~2 minutes', 'record_commit', 'refs/heads/moe/control', 'commit in the control checkout', 'in either mode', 'MOE_AGENT_GIT_REFUSED', 'lastCommitOutcome', 'counts toward the reopen cap', 'Landing gap:', '#governors'), and never write a retired or forbidden phrase: 'shared mode only' (so never 'in shared mode only'), 'land it yourself', 'you self-landed', 'Do NOT wait', 'wait for it before reviewing'. Same daemonGitDocs phrase ban as step 1. Do not touch .moe/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md: it is daemon-owned, the daemon refreshes stale marked copies at start, and worktree landings never carry .moe/ paths. Edit tool only. Error handling: doc-only; the sentinel test in step 4 fails loudly on a dropped or retired phrase.

Never cp, sed or redirect into the tracked file (no TOOL witness).
